description: Simulates five particles labelled A to E moving under invented laws of physics; the position of A goes in as three voltages and the positions of the other four come out as twelve

params.text: Sets the rate at which time flows in the simulation, from -6 to +6, each unit doubling it; low settings give slow control voltages and high settings give audible tones
Sets the friction that damps vibration; high settings ring on reverberantly and can build into strong oscillation, low settings die away into percussive or filtered sounds
Sets the strength of the magnetic force against the attractive and repulsive forces, from -1 to +1 with 0 turning it off; the two signs bend the motion in opposite directions
Sets how hard the A vector input drives the simulation; fully counter-clockwise the input has no effect at all
Sets the level of the twelve outputs, working together with the output limiter; it glows red while the limiter is reducing gain
Attenuates and inverts the speed CV
Attenuates and inverts the decay CV
Attenuates and inverts the magnetic coupling CV
Attenuates and inverts the input drive CV
Attenuates and inverts the output level CV
Switches between AUDIO mode, where the outputs pass through a DC-reject high-pass filter set to 30Hz by default, and CONTROL mode, where the raw position vectors reach the ports

inputs.text: The x coordinate of particle A; polyphonic channels are summed to one voltage
The y coordinate of particle A; polyphonic channels are summed to one voltage
The z coordinate of particle A; polyphonic channels are summed to one voltage

notes: every output is one channel, and every input sums its channels into a single voltage, which makes each input port a unity gain mixer
hovering to the right of a row's z output brings up a yellow box, and clicking it picks which particle a Tricorder on the right graphs
the particles start at rest and stay there: nothing moves and the twelve outputs hold fixed voltages until a changing signal reaches AX, AY or AZ.
menu: Output limiter — sets an automatic gain control threshold from 1V to 10V, 4V by default, or turns it off at the far right; the OUT knob glows red while it is reducing gain
DC reject cutoff — sets the high-pass corner used in AUDIO mode anywhere from 20Hz to 400Hz, 30Hz by default, which trims bass rumble
Reset simulation — returns the particles to that starting state, which recovers the module when it has gone unstable
Limiter warning light — turns off the red glow on the OUT knob without turning the limiter off
Toggle sensitivity on all attenuverters — divides the effect of every attenuverter on the panel by 10, or restores them all
Low sensitivity — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: divides that knob's effect by 10 and marks the knob with an orange dot
Unipolar mode — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: adds 5V to the CV on that control and clamps the result at zero
